authority_boundary: DAD context entries are candidate-only routing memory. They do not override local governance, Scripture authority, chunking authority, graph truth, retrieval truth, canon scope, source-tradition choice, or theology authority.

contexts.title: Whole-Bible Multi-Model Chunking Fork
contexts.extra_context: Experimental scratch-lane whole-Bible chunking marathons use separate model folders and require later governed comparison, frontier review, and owner gates before any output-changing use.

contexts.title: Scratch Delta Isolation Pattern For Hard Corpus Chunking
contexts.extra_context: The T423/T464 chunking fork uses isolated model outputs and a later comparison docket so agreement can reduce review search space and disagreement can surface hard decisions. Agreement remains evidence only; it cannot authorize chunks, reviewed gold, theology, source-tradition choice, or canon changes.

contexts.title: Rust Fast Validators And Rust-First Coding Preflight
contexts.extra_context: Rust is preferred for deterministic, high-resource leaf scanners and validators when data size, runtime, and maintenance tradeoffs justify it. Python remains the governance orchestrator.

contexts.title: DAD Lesson Slot Integrity For Rust Validator Assets
contexts.extra_context: If an outbox row reports a reusable lesson or asset to DAD, the referenced lesson slot and context-map entry must be present and validated so dirty parallel repo work does not create dangling DAD references.

contexts.title: Runtime Environment Preflight For Sandbox Temp And Cargo Failures
contexts.extra_context: Windows/Codex desktop sandbox runs can fail validators from temp-dir or Cargo target access before repo code is actually evaluated. The source repo records repo-local pytest basetemp, TMP/TEMP, and CARGO_TARGET_DIR routing as reusable preflight context while preserving local validation authority.

contexts.title: Scout-Guided Rust Canonical QA Leaf Validator
contexts.extra_context: T457 used separate read-only Rust architecture and QA/governance scouts to choose a Rust slice by fit. The selected slice streams high-volume canonical JSONL sidecars in Rust while Python remains the governance wrapper and DAD/task authority surface.

contexts.title: AI-Agnostic Rust Subagent Charter
contexts.extra_context: T458 records that Rust work should use capability-profile subagents for architecture, outside research, engineering, QA, and DAD reporting. Scout findings remain candidate-only, Python/pytest remain governance orchestration, and DAD cannot override local authority.

contexts.title: Scout-Guided Rust Word-Token Signal Scanner
contexts.extra_context: T459 follows the T458 AI-agnostic Rust subagent charter: a Rust architecture/outside research scout selected the large canonical word_tokens JSONL signal scan as a high-value Rust slice, and a QA/DAD scout required no-text summaries, fail-closed Rust behavior, parity tests, and candidate-only DAD reporting.

contexts.title: Rust And DAD Stack Integration
contexts.extra_context: T460 records the ordered integration pattern for T456-T459: preserve append-only DAD rows by union, use an explicit integration task scope for stacked PRs, validate local DAD slots, and do not clean or mutate central DAD state from a source repo.

contexts.title: Validation Gate Lifecycle Registry
contexts.extra_context: T460 records a lifecycle registry pattern for validators and adjacent operational contracts: active, active_generated_data, shadow, superseded, retired, replacement gate, retirement criteria, and generated-data missing-input behavior.

contexts.title: PR Queue Hygiene And Stale Branch Escalation
contexts.extra_context: T423 integration exposed the cost of many AI-created branches/PRs sitting unmerged while more work accumulated. The reusable lesson is to record next-action state, escalate stale PRs to a human/integrator, and use explicit integration branches rather than letting queues turn into conflict archaeology.

contexts.title: Modular Rust Validator Bundle
contexts.extra_context: T462 records the preferred shape for combining deterministic Rust validation checks: short dispatcher main.rs, named modules with run_check(input) -> CheckReport, and a bundle command that preserves per-check names, timings, and failure messages.

contexts.title: AI Draft PR Lifecycle And Rust Validator Strategy
contexts.extra_context: T463 records two repo hygiene patterns for DAD reuse: AI-created draft work must reach PR or an owner-visible exit state, and repeated deterministic Python validators can keep stable Python commands while delegating expensive scans to modular Rust CheckReport leaf checks.

contexts.title: Multi-Model Reconciliation Gate Before Owner Decisions
contexts.extra_context: T465 records a reusable pattern for dirty multi-agent scratch pipelines: freeze and validate comparison evidence, triage harness failures, packetize specialist cases like Mark 16, and surface owner dockets without letting model agreement become reviewed gold or output authority.

contexts.title: Model-Panel Provenance Correction And Harness Root-Cause Lessons
contexts.extra_context: T472 documents why multi-model agreement can fail: ambiguous region/span lineage, count-only validation, correlated chapter anchors, mechanically distorted harness outputs, and manifest/progress drift. It recommends typed provenance, semantic invariants, preserved negative controls, overlap checks, and proposer-critic-frontier-owner correction. It corrects the older T465 preferred-pair routing lesson.

contexts.title: Source Marker Anchor And Gold Integrity
contexts.extra_context: A parser's implicit current-record state can make generated output, tests, gold, and hashes consistently wrong. DAD should promote explicit anchor types, independent raw-order checks, layer-leakage gates, and staged shadow regeneration as reusable assets.

contexts.title: M7 Whole-Bible Chunking Replay And Audit Lessons
contexts.extra_context: The M7 partial whole-Bible campaign showed that exact coverage and many role-separated reviews do not replace official schema validation, final-state synchronization, explicit shared-model-substrate disclosure, provisional-before-premortem adjudication, cross-form calibration, and receipt-last hashing.
